findings.text: Jump condition evaluation provides a total mapping from operation code plus two operands to a boolean outcome. Bit test succeeds when the operands overlap in at least one bit position. Equality and inequality follow direct comparison. One ordering family interprets both operands as unsigned for greater, greater or equal, less and less or equal. A parallel family interprets both as signed for the same four relations. The unsigned family uses plain ordering mnemonics while the signed family uses variants marked as signed. Codes outside these families yield false.

Jump test emitters share a dual mode contract keyed on whether an output buffer is supplied. Without a buffer they only report the number of instruction slots the sequence would occupy, with distinct small fixed sizes per width and operand kind. With a buffer they populate exactly that many slots with a self contained test that stages operands in scratch registers, performs a single conditional transfer under test, reconciles taken versus not taken flow with an unconditional transfer when needed, and terminates. Narrow forms base expectation on narrowed operands while wide forms use full width values. One immediate form additionally seeds the result register from the expected outcome.

Width specific fill helpers adapt a shared pattern generator to jump testing. Each helper fixes destination and source widths, selects the same pair of pattern blocks, and binds the matching emitter for its width and operand kind. Immediate helpers combine wide destinations with narrow sources while register helpers use wide widths for both sides. All helpers forward the caller operation code opaquely and return the generator status.

Eleven full width immediate fill entries each dedicate the generic immediate helper to one condition, covering bit test, equality, inequality, unsigned ordering and signed ordering. Each entry accepts only the test descriptor and returns the helper outcome, differing solely in the condition selected.

Eleven narrowed immediate fill entries each dedicate the generic narrowed immediate helper to one condition across the same condition set. Each entry accepts only the test descriptor and returns the helper outcome.

Eleven full width register fill entries each dedicate the generic register helper to one condition across the same condition set. Each entry accepts only the test descriptor and returns the helper outcome.

Eleven narrowed register fill entries each dedicate the generic narrowed register helper to one condition across the same condition set. Each entry accepts only the test descriptor and returns the helper outcome.

Maximum staggered jump chain extent is bounded by scaling the largest encodable branch displacement down by a factor of three and forcing the result to an even number, keeping generated staggered sequences within reachable offsets.
The configured number of staggered jump runs is ten.

Staggered program synthesis derives its chain extent from the expected result recorded in the test descriptor and allocates a matching instruction array. The image contains an initialization header that clears the result register, stages two operand registers from caller values and enters near the middle of the body, followed by a repeated three slot body and a single terminating slot. Each body element first guards on the evolving result, then advances the result to a position derived magnitude, then replays the caller supplied jump template with a rewritten displacement linking elements into a staggered forward and backward chain without zero displacement links. Allocation failure leaves descriptor outputs untouched and reports an out of memory status.

Execution of a synthesized staggered image progresses through initialization, a deterministic walk across the staggered chain, and termination. The result register starts cleared, is compared against position derived expectations at each visited element, and is updated to the visited magnitude before the rewritten jump redirects to another element. The walk continues until control reaches the terminating slot, yielding the chain extent plus one as observable outcome.
Unconditional staggered entry exercises the staggered synthesizer with an always taken jump template and zeroed operands.

Eleven staggered full width immediate entries each pair one condition with immediate and register values chosen to satisfy it, so the exercised jump is always taken during the staggered walk. Cases include matching values for equality, mismatched values for inequality, overlapping masks for bit test, large versus small values for unsigned ordering, and negative values around minus one and minus two for signed ordering.

Eleven staggered full width register entries each pair one condition with two register values chosen to satisfy it, exercising the taken path for the same condition set as the immediate staggered family.
Eleven staggered narrowed immediate entries each pair one narrowed condition with satisfying immediate and register values, exercising the taken path for the narrowed width.
Eleven staggered narrowed register entries each pair one narrowed condition with two satisfying register values, exercising the taken path for the narrowed width.

Observed classic test descriptors combine a human readable name, a fixed instruction list, execution flags, an optional packet byte sequence, and a set of input length to expected result pairs. Flags indicate classic interpretation and whether packet data is required. Instruction lists exercise load, arithmetic, transfer and return operations across immediate, register and packet addressing modes.

Chain extent and allocation size are computed directly from the expected result field, so an incorrect or hostile descriptor value propagates into memory allocation scale and loop bounds before any validation visible in these fragments.

Rewritten displacements depend on position arithmetic with sign adjustment and scaling, plus a middle entry offset. Any mismatch in scaling or entry calculation would direct test execution outside the synthesized image.
